meta.title: Open-meetings notice and public-records response, by state (research draft)
meta.gatheredBy: Laws and effects session, four research helpers
meta.status: DRAFT, ESTIMATED: every figure comes from web-search result text, never from a statute page read in full (page fetches were blocked in the cloud container). The quote fields are fragments the search results showed, some of them a search tool's paraphrase. Check a row against the statute before it sets a law. No reader yet: the meetings and legislature engines keep no notice period, so this file sits in docs/research and is not data/research.
meta.noticeHours: Minimum advance public notice before a REGULAR meeting of a local public body, hours; null where the law sets no number (reasonable notice only). 32 of 56 have a number.
meta.recordsDays: Days to respond to a public-records request; recordsDayKind says business or calendar; null where the law says only promptly or reasonable time. 43 of 56 have a number.
meta.weakRows: TX (72 hours approximates a 2025 rule of three business days), VA (72 approximates three working days), WI (24-hour notice not found), PR (records may be 20 business days under Ley 156-2025), GU (records sources disagree), MP (72 hours from a college policy citing the Act), ID and LA (check first), AK and HI (records rules cover state agencies only / a rule not the statute), CA (10 calendar days to decide, not to produce), WY (7 business or 30 calendar days, sources conflict).

noticeHours.rule: a place with no number uses the median of those with one (noticeHoursUsed); noticeHoursEstimate says so

recordsDays.rule: same for records days (recordsDaysUsed); business and calendar days are mixed in the median, recordsDayKind says which each place is

US-AK.noticeNote: AS 44.62.310 requires only 'reasonable public notice'; no number.
US-AK.recordsNote: 10 working days for initial response comes from regulation 2 AAC 96.325 (state executive agencies), not the statute; extendable by 10 working days. Does not reach every public body.
US-AK.quote: a state agency in the executive branch has 10 working days to provide an initial response
US-AK.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-AL.noticeNote: 7 days for regular meeting; 24 hours special; 1 hour emergency (secondary guide summary of 36-25A-3).
US-AL.recordsNote: Act 2024-278: acknowledge within 10 business days, substantive response within 15 business days (guides differ on whether 15 runs from acknowledgment); 45 business days for time-intensive requests.
US-AL.quote: seven days' notice prior to a regular meeting, 24 hours for a 'special meeting,' and no less than one hour for an 'emergency meeting'

US-AR.noticeNote: Regular meetings: only the time and place must be furnished to anyone who requests; no advance-hours number. Special/emergency meetings: notice at least 2 hours before, to requesting news media.
US-AR.recordsNote: 3 working days if record in active use or storage; failure to respond is treated as denial.
US-AR.quote: Failure of the custodian to respond within three working days shall be considered a denial of the request
US-AR.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-AS.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).
US-AS.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).

US-AZ.noticeNote: 24 hours before meeting; Sundays and legal holidays do not count. Emergency exception for actual emergencies.
US-AZ.recordsNote: Statute says custodian shall 'promptly' furnish records; no fixed days. A bill to set five business days (HB2808, 2023) was not shown enacted.
US-AZ.quote: Access to a public record is deemed denied if a custodian fails to promptly respond to a request for production of a public record
US-AZ.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).

US-CA.noticeNote: Agenda posted at least 72 hours before a regular meeting (Brown Act). Special meetings 24 hours.
US-CA.recordsNote: 10 days to determine whether records are disclosable and notify requester; extendable 14 days; production only 'promptly' after. AB 1821 (2026) would convert to business days, status unconfirmed.
US-CA.quote: a regular meeting requires an agenda posted at least 72 hours beforehand

US-CO.noticeNote: Posting in designated public place or on website at least 24 hours before is deemed full and timely notice; statute says 'full and timely' generally.
US-CO.recordsNote: Three working days or less presumed reasonable; extension for extenuating circumstances up to 7 more working days.
US-CO.quote: a 'reasonable time' shall be presumed to be three working days or less

US-CT.noticeNote: Agenda for each regular meeting available at least 24 hours before; annual schedule of regular meetings filed with town clerk by Jan 31. Special meeting notice 24 hours.
US-CT.recordsNote: Agency must deny/respond within 4 business days or silence can be treated as denial (10 business days for certain 1-214 requests).
US-CT.quote: Each agency must make available its agenda for each regular meeting at least 24 hours before the meeting to which it refers.

US-DC.noticeNote: At least 48 hours or 2 business days, whichever is greater (OOG training text, quoted for electronic meetings); emergency: notice when members are notified.
US-DC.recordsNote: 15 days excluding Saturdays, Sundays, holidays; extendable 10 business days.
US-DC.quote: all public bodies are required to respond to a FOIA request within 15 business-days

US-DE.noticeNote: Seven days for notice and agenda; agenda late additions at least 6 hours before with reasons stated.
US-DE.recordsNote: Respond as soon as possible, within 15 business days; extension notice allowed.
US-DE.quote: as soon as possible, but in any event within 15 business days

US-FL.noticeNote: Statute requires only 'reasonable notice'; no hours. An agency guide says seven days is accepted informally, not statutory.
US-FL.recordsNote: NOT FOUND in search results; Chapter 119 not retrieved. No fixed day count shown.
US-FL.quote: provide reasonable notice of all such meetings
US-FL.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).
US-FL.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).

US-GA.noticeNote: Per secondary guides: 24 hours posted for regular meetings; special meetings 24 hours (shorter allowed for emergencies with legal organ notice). Not confirmed against statute text.
US-GA.recordsNote: Records must be produced or a response given within three business days of receipt.
US-GA.quote: an agency must produce records responsive to a request within three business days absent exceptional circumstances

US-GU.noticeNote: P.L. 24-109 amended 8107: five working days public notice plus second notice at least 48 hours before meeting. Emergency waiver. Current codified text not read.
US-GU.recordsNote: Third-party summary and legislative record: 4 working days (5 GCA 10103(d)), unusual-circumstance extension; sources inconsistent, verify.
US-GU.quote: five working days public notice, and a second public notice at least forty-eight (48) hours prior to the start of the meeting

US-HI.noticeNote: Notice filed and posted at least six calendar days before the meeting; emergency meetings excepted.
US-HI.recordsNote: Deadline comes from administrative rule HAR 2-71-13: fully disclosable records within reasonable time not exceeding 10 business days; longer with acknowledgment.
US-HI.statute: Haw. Rev. Stat. 92-7; Haw. Admin. R. 2-71-13
US-HI.quote: at least six calendar days before the meeting

US-IA.noticeNote: Notice posted at least 24 hours before the meeting with date, time, place, tentative agenda; waivable only if impossible or impractical (emergency).
US-IA.recordsNote: 22.8 delay ordinarily should not exceed 10 business days, never more than 20 calendar days; context is good-faith delay, not a flat response deadline.
US-IA.quote: The delay shall not exceed 20 calendar days and ordinarily should not exceed 10 business days.

US-ID.noticeNote: Regular meetings: 5 calendar days notice (120 h) plus agenda 48 h before; special meetings 24 h unless emergency. Read from search-result summaries of the AG/county open-meeting manuals.
US-ID.recordsNote: Grant or deny within 3 working days; if more time needed, up to 10 working days with written notice; nonresident window described as 21 days.
US-ID.quote: Regular meetings require notice five calendar days in advance and an agenda 48 hours before the meeting; agency must either grant or deny a resident's request to examine or copy public records within three working days.

US-IL.noticeNote: Agenda posted at least 48 hours before regular meeting; special/rescheduled meetings 48 hours; emergency as soon as practicable.
US-IL.recordsNote: Five business days to respond; extendable 5 more business days.
US-IL.quote: shall be given at least 48 hours before such meeting

US-IN.noticeNote: 48 hours before meeting, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays; may be disregarded in emergency.
US-IN.recordsNote: No fixed number: in-person requests 24 hours per PAC materials; other requests 'reasonable period of time'. Seven-day mail deadline not verified.
US-IN.quote: Public notice of the date, time, and place of meetings ... must be given at least forty-eight hours before the meeting, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays.
US-IN.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).

US-KS.noticeNote: KOMA requires notice to those who request it, reasonable in manner and timing; no number of hours.
US-KS.recordsNote: Request acted upon as soon as possible, not later than end of 3rd business day following receipt (per AG guide).
US-KS.quote: not later than the end of the 3rd business day following date request is received - K.S.A. 45-218(d)
US-KS.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-KY.noticeNote: KRS 61.820 requires only that a schedule of regular meetings be made available to the public; no hours number found.
US-KY.recordsNote: Since HB 312 (June 29, 2021) agency must respond within 5 business days; formerly 3.
US-KY.quote: HB 312 amends KRS 61.880(1) so that after June 29, 2021, a public agency must respond to a request to inspect records within five business days.
US-KY.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-LA.noticeNote: 24 hours exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays for written notice/agenda posting; sources emphasize special or rescheduled meetings. Regular-meeting rule not separately confirmed.
US-LA.recordsNote: R.S. 44:32(D) three days exclusive of weekends/holidays when custodian questions status; 44:33 records in use: within 3 business days; 44:35 five-day time estimate. Sources inconsistent; lower confidence.
US-LA.quote: within three days, exclusive of Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays

US-MA.noticeNote: 48 hours before meeting excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays.
US-MA.recordsNote: 10 business days following receipt; supervisor may grant single extension (agency up to 20, municipality up to 30 business days).
US-MA.quote: a public body shall post notice of every meeting at least 48 hours prior to the meeting, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays

US-MD.noticeNote: 'Reasonable advance notice' only; no fixed number; Compliance Board found one-day notice insufficient.
US-MD.recordsNote: Grant or deny promptly and no later than 30 days; if more than 10 working days needed, notice within that period; applicant may consent to 30 more days.
US-MD.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-ME.noticeNote: Public notice 'in a manner reasonably calculated to notify the general public'; no hours number.
US-ME.recordsNote: Acknowledge request within 5 working days and give good-faith estimate of time; production time not fixed. Denial in writing within 5 working days.
US-ME.quote: acknowledge receipt of a request made according to this section within 5 working days of receiving the request
US-ME.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-MI.noticeNote: Regular meetings: yearly schedule posted within 10 days after first meeting of year; no per-meeting hours. Special and rescheduled regular meetings: 18 hours.
US-MI.recordsNote: Respond within 5 business days; one extension of up to 10 business days (15 total).
US-MI.quote: for a rescheduled regular or a special meeting of a public body, a public notice stating the date, time, and place of the meeting shall be posted at least 18 hours before the meeting.
US-MI.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-MN.noticeNote: Regular meeting schedule kept on file at primary office; no hours number. Special meetings: posted notice (3 days if published).
US-MN.recordsNote: Data Practices Act requires prompt and reasonable response; Rule 1205.0300 reasonable time; no number.
US-MN.quote: A schedule of the regular meetings of a public body shall be kept on file at its primary offices.
US-MN.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).
US-MN.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).

US-MO.noticeNote: Notice with tentative agenda at least 24 hours before meeting (as much as reasonably possible if impractical).
US-MO.recordsNote: Act as soon as possible, no later than third business day; if production takes longer, respond in that window with estimate and reason.
US-MO.quote: requests be acted upon as soon as possible, but no later than the third business day following receipt

US-MP.noticeNote: Only secondary: NMC board policy cites 1 CMC 9910 for 72 hours notice of regular meetings (24 hours for special agendas); statute text not read.
US-MP.recordsNote: Open Government Act: 10 days initial response, extendable 10 more; day kind not stated in sources.
US-MP.quote: public notification of all regular meetings of the Board shall be made 72 hours in advance of the meetings

US-MS.noticeNote: No fixed per-meeting hours found for regular meetings; special/recessed/interim meetings require posting within one hour of the call (25-41-13(1)(a)).
US-MS.recordsNote: Public bodies may not adopt procedures allowing production or denial later than 7 working days; written explanation may extend to 14 working days.
US-MS.quote: No public body shall adopt procedures which will authorize the public body to produce or deny production of a public record later than seven (7) working days from the date of the receipt of the request.
US-MS.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-MT.noticeNote: 2-3-103 requires adequate notice and published agenda for decisions of significant public interest; no hours number.
US-MT.recordsNote: Local governments: no fixed deadline ('timely'); executive agencies reportedly 5 business days under 2-6-1006(3); not confirmed in statute text.
US-MT.quote: The procedures must ensure adequate notice and assist public participation before a final agency action is taken (2-3-103(1), MCA).
US-MT.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).
US-MT.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).

US-NC.noticeNote: Regular meetings: current schedule kept on file/posted, no hours. Meetings off the filed schedule: 48 hours notice.
US-NC.recordsNote: G.S. 132-6(a) 'as promptly as possible'; no number of days.
US-NC.quote: This notice shall be posted and mailed, emailed, or delivered at least 48 hours before the time of the meeting.
US-NC.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).
US-NC.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).

US-ND.noticeNote: Notice required in advance but no numeric period found for regular meetings; special meetings also need notice to official newspaper/requesting media. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-ND.recordsNote: Statute says only a reasonable response; AG opinions treat delays of weeks as unreasonable; no number.
US-ND.quote: Unless otherwise provided by law, public notice must be given in advance
US-ND.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).
US-ND.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).

US-NE.noticeNote: 24 hours before meeting; emergency meetings allowed without reasonable public notice. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-NE.recordsNote: Four business days after receipt, excluding the day received; written explanation if more time needed.
US-NE.quote: public notice of meetings at least 24 hours in advance

US-NH.noticeNote: 24 hours, not counting Sundays or holidays; emergency meetings need not meet it. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-NH.recordsNote: Five business days to provide, deny in writing, or acknowledge with time needed.
US-NH.quote: at least 24 hours' notice before a meeting, not counting Sundays or holidays

US-NJ.noticeNote: 48 hours written advance notice; not needed for genuine emergencies; annual notice may cover regular meetings. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-NJ.recordsNote: Seven business days after receipt or deemed denial; extensions need agreement/state-of-emergency relaxation.
US-NJ.quote: written advance notice of at least 48 hours, giving the time, date, location and, to the extent known, the agenda

US-NM.noticeNote: Agenda must be posted at least 72 hours before meeting (2013 amendment); regular-meeting notice also set by annual resolution; emergency exception. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-NM.recordsNote: Inspection immediately or no later than 15 calendar days; written response within 3 business days if not granted.
US-NM.quote: no later than fifteen (15) calendar days after the records custodian receives the inspection request

US-NV.noticeNote: Written notice at least 3 working days before meeting (posted by 9 a.m. of third working day), so 72 hours is an approximation of working days; emergency exception. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-NV.recordsNote: Respond in writing by end of fifth business day (provide, deny, or notice of more time).
US-NV.quote: written notice must be given at least 3 working days before the meeting

US-NY.noticeNote: At least 72 hours for meetings scheduled a week or more ahead; reasonable time for shorter-notice meetings. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-NY.recordsNote: Written response (grant, deny, or acknowledge) within 5 business days; up to 20 business days more after acknowledgement with stated date.
US-NY.quote: not less than seventy-two hours prior to the meeting

US-OH.noticeNote: No set advance period for regular meetings; body sets its own notice rule; special meeting 24 hours; emergency immediate. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-OH.recordsNote: Prompt inspection, copies within a reasonable period; no fixed days.
US-OH.quote: Ohio does not impose specific requirements for how far in advance notice must be given
US-OH.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).
US-OH.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).

US-OK.noticeNote: Regular meeting agenda posted 24 hours ahead (search summary says '24 or 48 hours' depending on meeting type; special meeting notice 48 hours, agenda 24); annual schedule filed in advance. Verify. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-OK.quote: Notice posted 48 hours in advance and agenda posted 24 hours prior to meeting
US-OK.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).

US-OR.noticeNote: Regular meetings require only 'reasonable notice'; special meetings at least 24 hours (ORS 192.640(3)). Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-OR.recordsNote: Acknowledge within 5 business days; complete as soon as reasonably possible or within 15 business days, whichever is sooner.
US-OR.quote: complete the response as soon as reasonably possible or within fifteen business days from receipt
US-OR.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-PA.noticeNote: Sunshine Act 3-day newspaper notice applies to first regular meeting plus the annual schedule, not each regular meeting; agenda posted 24 hours before (c.1); emergency meetings no notice. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-PA.recordsNote: Initial 5 business day response with extension option invoked within that window.
US-PA.quote: the schedule must be published at least three days before the first regular meeting
US-PA.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-PR.noticeNote: NOT FOUND for municipal legislatures (Codigo Municipal, Ley 107-2020 not read).
US-PR.recordsNote: Ley 141-2019 art. 7: 10 dias laborables (extendable). Ley 156-2025 may raise central offices to 20; not confirmed.
US-PR.quote: diez (10) días laborables para la entrega de la información, según establece el art. 7 de la Ley Núm. 141-2019
US-PR.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-RI.noticeNote: 48 hours excluding weekends and state holidays; emergency meetings with stated reason. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-RI.recordsNote: Ten business days; extension of 20 more business days for good cause.
US-RI.quote: at least 48 hours prior to the meeting, excluding weekend and state holidays

US-SC.noticeNote: Agenda/notice posted at least 24 hours before regular or special meeting. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-SC.recordsNote: 10 business days if records two years old or less; 20 for older; production within 30 calendar days of response.
US-SC.quote: 10 business days to respond to written FOIA request if documents are two years old or less

US-SD.noticeNote: Political subdivisions post notice and agenda for a continuous 24 hours; state bodies 72 hours. Page fetch was blocked in this session; figures come from WebSearch result text only.
US-SD.recordsNote: Initial response within 10 business days per SDCL 1-27-37 (secondary summary; verify).
US-SD.quote: posted for a continuous 24 hours before the meeting

US-TN.noticeNote: Act does not define adequate public notice; no number of hours. Applies to regular and special meetings.
US-TN.recordsNote: Custodian has seven business days to produce, deny in writing, or give a written estimate if the record cannot be produced promptly.
US-TN.quote: Adequate public notice is not defined in the Tennessee Open Meetings Act.
US-TN.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-TX.noticeNote: HB 1522 (2025, eff. Sept 1 2025) amended Gov't Code 551.043(a) from 72 hours to three business days; 72 used as the minimum-hours equivalent. Verify exact text.
US-TX.recordsNote: Must produce promptly; if not producible within 10 business days, certify in writing with a date. Also 10 business days to ask the AG for a decision.
US-TX.quote: If you cannot produce information within 10 business days after the date the information is requested, you must certify that fact in writing to the requestor

US-UT.noticeNote: At least 24 hours notice before a meeting; emergency meetings excepted when unforeseen circumstances arise.
US-UT.recordsNote: As soon as reasonably possible, no later than 10 business days after a written request; 5 business days if the requester shows expedited response benefits the public.
US-UT.quote: a public body shall give at least 24 hours notice before a meeting

US-VA.noticeNote: Statute (per a citizen's guide, not read in statute text) requires notice at least three working days before the meeting; 72 is an approximation of 3 days. Special and emergency meetings have flexibility.
US-VA.recordsNote: Five working days from receipt (day after receipt is Day 1); a further seven working days if the response is made within the first five.
US-VA.quote: A public body must respond within five working days of receipt of the request. NOTE: Count the day after receipt as Day 1.

US-VI.noticeNote: NOT FOUND: 1 V.I.C. 254 governs open meetings but no notice period seen.
US-VI.recordsNote: Sunshine Act (3 V.I.C. 881) reported to have no time limit for responding.
US-VI.quote: Title 3, § 881, currently contains no time limit for responding to records requests
US-VI.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).
US-VI.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).

US-VT.noticeNote: Agenda posted at least 48 hours before a regular meeting; 24 hours before a special meeting; emergency meetings need only notice as soon as practicable.
US-VT.recordsNote: 'Promptly' defined as not more than three business days unless otherwise provided; extensions available.
US-VT.quote: "promptly" means immediately, with little or no delay, and, unless otherwise provided in this section, not more than three business days.

US-WA.noticeNote: OPMA sets no special notice for regular meetings (time set by ordinance/resolution/bylaws); agenda online 24h before under RCW 42.30.077; special meetings 24 hours (RCW 42.30.080).
US-WA.recordsNote: Initial response within five business days (confirm acknowledgment vs produce; agency may state time needed).
US-WA.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-WI.noticeNote: 24-hour notice under 19.84(3) was NOT confirmed by any page read in this pass; not recorded.
US-WI.recordsNote: Statute: act as soon as practicable and without delay; no fixed number. DOJ policy treats 10 business days as generally reasonable for simple requests.
US-WI.quote: as soon as practicable and without delay
US-WI.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).
US-WI.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).

US-WV.noticeNote: Open Meetings Act requires agencies to set rules for advance notice; no fixed number. Ethics Commission guidance suggests three business days for bodies with no fixed schedule.
US-WV.recordsNote: Five days not counting Saturdays, Sundays or legal holidays to produce, arrange inspection, or deny in writing.
US-WV.quote: within five days, not counting Saturdays, Sundays or legal holidays
US-WV.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).

US-WY.noticeNote: Regular meetings set by ordinance/resolution/bylaws; AG summary says fair and reasonable advance notice. Special meetings 24 hours (16-4-404(b)); 8 hours media notice for rescheduled.
US-WY.recordsNote: NOT FOUND: sources conflict (7 business days acknowledgment vs 30 calendar days); statute text not read.
US-WY.quote: fair and reasonable advance notice of meetings
US-WY.noticeHoursEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 32 places that have one (48 hours; middle half 24 to 72).
US-WY.recordsDaysEstimate: ESTIMATED FROM AVERAGE: this place's law sets no number I could read, so the median of the 43 places that have one (5 days; middle half 4.5 to 10).
